deliverables: Constitute two advisory councils with charters, COI policies, named members, and published meeting records
Form a dOSPO 501(c)(3) public charity and publish governance documents
Publish quarterly public outcome reports with Mill Law Firm financial review attached
Run a dependency audit with SBOMs, centrality scores, bus factor assessments, and coverage gap analysis
Fund maintenance retainers for selected Cardano open source infrastructure projects
Launch a public CHAOSS-aligned dashboard for funded projects
Operate maintainer development, CodeForUs bounty, and ecosystem activation programs
request.recipient: Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting, with a target transition to a dOSPO 501(c)(3) public charity subject to governance/legal process
request.what: Establish a one-year independent Cardano dOSPO and Open Maintenance Framework program to manage open source sustainability funding, maintenance retainers, contributor development, bounties, ecosystem activation, governance infrastructure, and reporting.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 4,094,000 ADA over 12 months for a Cardano dOSPO and OMF program.
Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting is designated as the sole Article II.7.5 administrator at the moment of treasury withdrawal.
Mill Law Firm is designated as the independent financial auditor on a quarterly cadence through month 12.
Final allocation authority resides with the designated administrator, while advisory council feedback is published before disbursements.
The program will use four programs: a Maintenance Fund, a Maintainer Development program, a CodeForUs bounty program, and an Ecosystem Activation Reserve.
The Maintenance Fund will deploy 2,000,000 ADA over 12 months to support high-risk Cardano open source infrastructure selected through dependency data.
The proposal claims selection will follow published dependency centrality data rather than relationships.
The proposer claims there are 90 pages of whitepapers vetted by experts explaining how the structure will operate.
The proposer claims a strong ecosystem track record from prior open source governance and OSPO work at Intersect.
The proposal sets KPI targets including funding 40% of top-50 dependencies by month 12, four quarterly reports, maintainer attrition below 15%, and security response assessment under 48 hours.

summary: The document describes a 4,094,000 ADA, 12-month treasury-funded dOSPO/OMF program administered initially by Christian Taylor / Open Source Cowboy Consulting, with advisory councils, legal-entity formation, quarterly reporting, maintenance funding, dependency analysis, and open source sustainability programs.
